reason.description: Optional reason provided by the super administrator for the role change action.
reason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_admin_promotions.reason. Nullable string.

IEcommerceMallAdminPromotion.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to ecommerce_mall_admin_promotions table. sellerId.x-autobe-specification: Maps to ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions.ecommerce_mall_seller_id column. Must reference an existing seller in ecommerce_mall_sellers table. Format: UUID.

IEcommerceMallSellerSuspension.ICreate.description: Request body for suspending a seller account on the e-commerce platform. Contains the seller identifier and a mandatory reason for the suspension action.

reason.description: Optional reason for the promotion action, typically used for audit purposes. Can be null if no reason is provided.

IEcommerceMallAdminPromotion.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: reason (optional). The admin_id is extracted from path parameter adminId. IEcommerceMallProductVariantOptionValue..description: Request body for updating product variant option values. Contains the option key (name) and value to set. Used for both bulk upsert (PATCH) and single update (PUT) operations.
IEcommerceMallProductVariantOptionValue..x-autobe-specification: Maps to key and value columns in ecommerce_mall_product_variant_option_values table. IEcommerceMallReview.IRequest.description: Pagination parameters for retrieving review edit history snapshots. Controls the page number and maximum records per page for paginated listing of review modification history.
IEcommerceMallReview.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Pagination request parameters for querying review snapshots. Source: ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots filtered by reviewId from path parameter. This DTO provides query control parameters only - the actual data retrieval happens from the review_snapshots table. Downstream agents should use page and limit values to compute OFFSET and LIMIT for SQL queries.

id.description: Unique identifier of the review snapshot.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots.id. UUID primary key.

rating.description: Star rating value (1-5) of the review before this edit was made.

body.description: Text content of the review before this edit was made. Null if the review had no text content.
body.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots.body. Nullable string.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing when the review edit occurred.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time.

review.description: Parent review this snapshot captures, showing the review state at the time of snapshot creation.
review.x-autobe-specification: Belongs-to relation via ecommerce_mall_review_id FK. Nested ISummary object replaces the raw FK ID. Circular prevention: review ISummary excludes reviewSnapshots array.

IEcommerceMallReview.IInvert.description: Immutable historical snapshot of a review's previous state at the time of an edit, including the parent review context for reference. Serves as audit trail for dispute resolution when customers contest product conditions at purchase time.
IEcommerceMallReview.IInvert.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots table. JOIN with ecommerce_mall_reviews on ecommerce_mall_review_id to populate nested review ISummary. FK column replaced by belongs-to relation exposed as nested object.

customer.description: The customer who initiated the refund request.
customer.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.ecommerce_mall_customer_id to ecommerce_mall_customers.id. Returns IEcommerceMallCustomer.ISummary with display name and profile.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created, marking when the seller responded.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.created_at. Timestamp when snapshot was created (coincides with seller response moment).

id.description: Unique identifier of the refund request snapshot.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.id. UUID primary key.

refundRequest.description: The parent refund request this snapshot belongs to.
refundRequest.x-autobe-specification: Direct reference from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.ecommerce_mall_refund_request_id to ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.id. Returns IEcommerceMallRefundRequest.ISummary.

seller.description: The seller who responded to the refund request.
seller.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.ecommerce_mall_seller_id to ecommerce_mall_sellers.id. Returns IEcommerceMallSeller.ISummary with email and profile.

sellerResponse.description: The seller's response decision to the refund request.
sellerResponse.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.seller_response. Enum values: 'approved' or 'rejected'.

sellerResponseReason.description: Optional reason provided by the seller when rejecting the refund request.
sellerResponseReason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.seller_response_reason. Nullable - present only when seller_response is 'rejected'.

sellerResponseAt.description: Timestamp when the seller approved or rejected the refund request.
sellerResponseAt.x-autobe-specification: Computed from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.created_at. Snapshot is created precisely when seller responds, so snapshot creation time equals seller response time.

snapshotReason.description: The reason text submitted by the customer for the refund request at the time of snapshot creation.
snapshotReason.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.snapshot_reason. Customer's original reason text captured at snapshot creation.

snapshotStatus.description: The status of the refund request at the time of snapshot creation.
snapshotStatus.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.snapshot_status. Status value at snapshot creation time (e.g., pending, approved, rejected).

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was last updated.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots.updated_at. Timestamp when snapshot record was last modified.

IEcommerceMallRefundRequest.IInvert.description: Complete immutable snapshot of a refund request captured at the moment of seller response. Includes customer's original reason, status at snapshot time, seller's decision (approved/rejected), and optional rejection reason. Used as authoritative evidence during dispute resolution.
IEcommerceMallRefundRequest.IInvert.x-autobe-specification: Query ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table filtering by snapshotId (id) and requestId (ecommerce_mall_refund_request_id in path). Verify access rights: customers verify ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches JWT identity, sellers verify ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches JWT identity, admins/superAdmins grant full access. Return complete snapshot record with BELONGS-TO relations (customer, seller, refundRequest) resolved to ISummary types via JOIN queries. sellerResponseAt computed from created_at since snapshot is created precisely when seller responds.

id.description: Primary key of the metadata entry.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_log_metadata.id. UUID primary key.

key.description: Metadata property name identifying the type of metadata (e.g., previous_state, new_state, reason, target_entity_type).
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_log_metadata.key. Stores metadata property name.

value.description: Metadata property value containing the actual data for this metadata entry.
value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_log_metadata.value. Stores metadata property value.

IEcommerceMallSuperAdminAuditLogMetadatu.description: Summary representation of a super administrator audit log metadata entry for list display, showing key-value pairs of audit context.
IEcommerceMallSuperAdminAuditLogMetadatu.x-autobe-specification: Maps to ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_log_metadata table for audit trail metadata entries. Each entry represents a key-value pair of audit context (e.g., previous_state, new_state, reason, target_entity_type). Parent audit log accessed via IEcommerceMallSuperAdminAuditLogSummary reference, not included here.

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - E2E Test Requirements

## Authentication Tests

### Customer Authentication
- Test customer registration with valid email and password
- Test customer registration with invalid email format
- Test customer registration with weak password
- Test customer registration with duplicate email
- Test customer login with valid credentials
- Test customer login with invalid password
- Test customer login with non-existent email
- Test customer change password with correct current password
- Test customer change password with incorrect current password
- Test customer account deletion (verify orders preserved, reviews marked as deleted)

### Seller Authentication
- Test seller registration
- Test seller login
- Test seller approval status check (pending/approved/rejected)
- Test seller reregistration after rejection
- Test seller account deletion (only when no pending orders/refunds)
- Test seller account deletion blocked when pending orders exist

### Administrator Authentication
- Test admin request submission
- Test admin login
- Test super admin approval of admin request
- Test super admin rejection of admin request
- Test promotion to super admin
- Test demotion from super admin (cannot demote self)

## Customer Profile Tests
- Test get own profile
- Test update display name
- Test update phone number
- Test update with invalid data

## Address Management Tests
- Test add new address
- Test add address with missing required fields
- Test list addresses
- Test edit address
- Test delete address
- Test set default address
- Test delete default address (another becomes default)
- Test checkout with default address

## Seller Profile Tests
- Test get own profile
- Test update shop name (verify snapshot created)
- Test update shop description
- Test update logo
- Test view own snapshots
- Test public view of seller profile by customer

## Category Management Tests
- Test admin create category
- Test admin create subcategory
- Test admin edit category
- Test admin delete category (products become uncategorized)
- Test non-admin cannot create category
- Test customer browse categories
- Test customer view products in category

## Product Management Tests

### Product CRUD
- Test seller create product with all required fields
- Test seller create product with missing required fields
- Test seller edit product (verify snapshot created)
- Test seller delete product (only when no pending orders)
- Test delete product blocked when pending orders exist
- Test admin view any product snapshot
- Test admin delete product

### Product Images
- Test upload multiple images
- Test reorder images (first becomes thumbnail)
- Test delete image
- Test image included in snapshot

### Product Variants
- Test add variant with SKU, options, price, stock
- Test edit variant (verify snapshot created)
- Test delete variant (only when no pending orders)
- Test product visible but unavailable when no variants
- Test product purchasable when has at least one variant

### Inventory Management
- Test restock inventory (positive quantity)
- Test inventory adjustment (negative quantity)
- Test view inventory history
- Test inventory record created on order
- Test inventory record created on cancellation
- Test inventory record created on refund

### Product Search
- Test search by name
- Test search with category filter
- Test search with price range filter
- Test search with in-stock filter
- Test sort by newest
- Test sort by price low to high
- Test sort by price high to low
- Test pagination

### Product Listing
- Test product listing shows main image, name, price, seller name, rating
- Test price range shown when variants have different prices

### Product Detail
- Test product detail shows all images
- Test product detail shows all variants with stock status
- Test product detail shows reviews and average rating

## Wishlist Tests
- Test add product to wishlist
- Test add same product twice (no duplicate)
- Test view wishlist
- Test remove product from wishlist
- Test product auto-removed from wishlist when deleted
- Test pagination

## Shopping Cart Tests
- Test add variant to cart
- Test add same variant increases quantity (not duplicate)
- Test add different variant creates new line
- Test view cart with all details
- Test update item quantity
- Test remove item
- Test cart total calculation
- Test warning when stock less than cart quantity
- Test unavailable items marked when variant deleted
- Test unavailable items marked when out of stock

## Checkout Tests
- Test checkout with valid cart and address
- Test checkout blocked when unavailable items in cart
- Test checkout without address selection (use default)
- Test checkout with explicit address selection
- Test order summary shows all items, address, total
- Test shipping address locked after order

## Payment Tests
- Test successful payment creates order
- Test successful payment reduces stock
- Test successful payment clears cart
- Test successful payment creates order items with "paid" status
- Test successful payment creates snapshots of products/variants/sellers
- Test failed payment does not create order
- Test failed payment allows retry

## Order Tests

### Order History
- Test customer view orders (paginated, newest first)
- Test order list shows order number, date, total, status
- Test order detail shows items, address, shipments

### Order Item Status
- Test item status starts as "paid"
- Test item changes to "shipped" when shipped
- Test item changes to "delivered" when confirmed
- Test item changes to "cancelled" when cancelled
- Test item changes to "refunded" when refunded

### Order Status Calculation
- Test order status "paid" when all items paid
- Test order status "shipped" when any item shipped
- Test order status "delivered" when all items delivered
- Test order status "cancelled" when all items cancelled
- Test order status "refunded" when all items refunded
- Test order status "partially_completed" for mixed states

## Shipping Tests
- Test seller creates shipment with items and tracking
- Test shipment tracking shows carrier and tracking number
- Test all items in shipment change to "shipped"
- Test different sellers create separate shipments
- Test customer view shipment tracking
- Test customer confirm delivery
- Test confirm delivery changes items to "delivered"
- Test auto-delivery after 14 days

## Cancellation Tests
- Test customer request cancellation for paid item
- Test cancellation with reason
- Test cancellation blocked for shipped item
- Test seller approve cancellation
- Test seller reject cancellation
- Test approved cancellation creates snapshot
- Test approved cancellation refunds item
- Test approved cancellation restores stock
- Test remaining items continue processing
- Test all items cancelled makes order "cancelled"

## Refund Tests
- Test customer request refund for delivered item
- Test refund with reason
- Test refund blocked within 7 days of delivery
- Test refund blocked for non-delivered item
- Test seller approve refund
- Test seller reject refund
- Test approved refund creates snapshot
- Test approved refund processes refund
- Test approved refund restores stock
- Test remaining items unaffected
- Test all items refunded makes order "refunded"

## Review Tests
- Test customer write review for delivered item
- Test review with rating only
- Test review with rating and text
- Test review blocked for non-delivered item
- Test one review per product per order enforced
- Test review appears on product page
- Test reviews sorted newest first
- Test edit review creates snapshot
- Test delete review (snapshots preserved)
- Test average rating calculation (only non-deleted reviews)

## Seller Dashboard Tests
- Test dashboard shows total products
- Test dashboard shows total order items
- Test dashboard shows pending cancellation count
- Test dashboard shows pending refund count
- Test list order items filterable by status

## Administrator Tests

### Seller Management
- Test view pending seller approvals
- Test approve seller
- Test reject seller with reason
- Test suspend seller (products hidden)
- Test unsuspend seller (products visible again)
- Test suspended seller cannot create/edit products
- Test suspended seller can process existing orders

### Product Oversight
- Test admin view all products
- Test admin view any product snapshot
- Test admin delete any product

### Order Oversight
- Test admin view all orders
- Test admin force-cancel item
- Test admin force-cancel entire order
- Test admin force-refund item
- Test admin force-refund entire order
- Test force action restores stock

### User Management
- Test ban customer
- Test banned customer cannot login
- Test unban customer
- Test ban seller
- Test banned seller cannot login
- Test banned seller existing orders remain
- Test unban seller

## Snapshot Tests
- Test product edit creates snapshot with all fields
- Test variant edit creates snapshot
- Test seller profile edit creates snapshot
- Test review edit creates snapshot
- Test cancellation creates snapshot
- Test refund creates snapshot
- Test order item includes product/variant/seller snapshot
- Test snapshot immutable
- Test snapshot viewable by owner and admin

## Integration Tests

### Full Purchase Flow
1. Customer registers and logs in
2. Customer adds shipping address
3. Seller registers, gets approved
4. Seller creates product with variants
5. Seller sets inventory
6. Customer searches and finds product
7. Customer views product detail
8. Customer adds to wishlist
9. Customer adds to cart
10. Customer checks out
11. Customer pays
12. Order created with "paid" status
13. Seller ships order
14. Customer receives tracking
15. Customer confirms delivery
16. Customer writes review

### Multi-Item Order Flow
1. Customer adds items from multiple sellers
2. Order created with multiple order items
3. Each seller ships their items separately
4. Each shipment tracked independently
5. Customer confirms each delivery
6. Customer can cancel/refund individual items

### Cancellation Flow
1. Customer places order
2. Customer requests cancellation
3. Seller approves
4. Item cancelled
5. Stock restored
6. Refund processed
7. Remaining items continue

### Refund Flow
1. Customer receives delivery
2. Customer requests refund within 7 days
3. Seller approves
4. Item refunded
5. Stock restored

scenario.draft: Test the guest session establishment endpoint with valid fingerprint and navigation context. Submit a POST request with fingerprint, href (current page URL), and referrer (previous page URL). Validate the response contains: (1) HTTP 201 status, (2) guest UUID identifier, (3) JWT access token that is non-empty string, (4) JWT refresh token that is non-empty string, (5) access token expiration timestamp (expired_at) in ISO 8601 format, (6) session expiration timestamp (refreshable_until) in ISO 8601 format. Verify the access token has short lifetime (~15 minutes) and refresh token has longer lifetime (~7 days).

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /ecommerceMall/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Test that the system reuses existing guest session when the same fingerprint is provided. Submit two consecutive POST requests with identical fingerprint value. Validate that both requests succeed with HTTP 201 and return valid JWT tokens. Verify the returned guest ID remains consistent across both requests when the same fingerprint is used, confirming the system reuses the existing guest record instead of creating duplicates.

This test ensures the system can track guest browsing patterns for analytics and session recovery.

scenario.draft:
Test successful guest token refresh with a valid refresh token obtained from guest join.

1. Call POST /ecommerceMall/auth/guest/join to establish a new guest session and obtain access/refresh token pair
2. Extract the refreshToken from the join response
3. Call POST /ecommerceMall/auth/guest/refresh with the valid refreshToken in the request body
4. Include optional context fields (ip, href, referrer) for security tracking
5. Verify the response contains a new access token (shorter expiration) and optionally a new refresh token
6. Verify the expired_at timestamp is in the future
7. Verify the refreshable_until timestamp indicates the session's maximum duration
8. Verify the guest session ID remains the same for continued session continuity

2. Verify the response returns HTTP 401 status
3. Verify the error response contains 'token_invalid' error code
4. Verify the response body does not contain any tokens
5. Verify this also handles cases like tampered tokens or tokens belonging to deleted guests

Test creating a product variant with all valid fields including unique SKU code, option values (color=red, size=large), and initial stock quantity.

scenario.draft:
Test that a seller cannot add a variant to a product they do not own, expecting 403 Forbidden response.

**Preconditions:**
- Admin has created a category
- Seller A has registered and created Product A
- Seller B has registered (but does not own Product A)

**Test Steps:**
1. Authenticate as Seller B (who does NOT own Product A)
2. Call POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants where {productId} is Product A's ID
   - skuCode: "SKU-UNAUTHORIZED-001"
   - optionValues: [{key: "color", value: "green"}]
   - quantity: 25

**Expected Results:**
- HTTP 403 Forbidden response
- Error message indicates seller does not have permission to modify this product
- No variant is created for Product A

**Business Logic Validation:**
- Ownership verification ensures sellers can only manage their own products
- Variant operations (create, edit, delete) are protected by ownership checks
- Sellers cannot interfere with other sellers' product catalogs
- Product's parent relationship to seller is verified before allowing variant creation
- The system checks that ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id matches the authenticated seller

scenario.draft:
Test successful variant deletion by the owning seller when there are no pending orders, cancellation requests, or refund requests for that variant.

**Preconditions:**
- A seller has registered and obtained authentication tokens
- The seller has created a product with a valid categoryId
- The seller has created a product variant with SKU code, option values (e.g., color: red, size: large), and initial stock quantity

**Test Steps:**
1. Authenticate as the seller using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/seller/join
2. Create a product using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products with valid name, description, categoryId, and basePrice
3. Create a variant using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants with skuCode, optionValues array, and quantity
4. Verify the variant was created successfully by checking the response contains the variant with its ID
5. Delete the variant using DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}

**Expected Results:**
- Variant deletion returns 204 No Content with no response body
- Variant is soft-deleted (deleted_at timestamp set internally)
- Variant no longer appears in subsequent variant listings for the product
- Any order items that were previously created referencing this variant remain preserved for historical records
- Cart items referencing the deleted variant are marked as unavailable so customers are informed they can no longer purchase

scenario.draft:
Test that variant deletion is blocked when there are pending cancellation requests for order items of that variant.

**Preconditions:**
- SuperAdmin has created a category for product assignment
- Seller has registered and obtained authentication tokens
- Seller has created a product with a variant that has inventory
- A customer has purchased the variant (order item has 'paid' status)
- Customer has submitted a cancellation request with 'pending' status

**Test Steps:**
1. Authenticate as superAdmin using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/superAdmin/join
2. Create category using POST /ecommerceMall/superAdmin/categories
3. Authenticate as seller using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/seller/join
4. Create product using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products (with categoryId from step 2)
5. Create variant using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants
6. Set inventory using POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/inventory with positive quantity
7. Authenticate as customer using POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join
8. Create customer shipping address using POST /ecommerceMall/customer/customers/addresses
9. Add variant to cart using POST /ecommerceMall/customer/customers/cart/items
10. Complete checkout using POST /ecommerceMall/customer/payments/checkout
11. Customer creates cancellation request using POST /ecommerceMall/customer/cancellation-requests
12. Verify cancellation request has 'pending' status
13. Attempt to delete the variant using DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}

**Expected Results:**
- Variant deletion returns 400 Bad Request
- Error message indicates that the variant cannot be deleted due to pending cancellation requests
- Variant remains active in the system
- Cancellation request remains pending

scenario.draft:
Test removing an available cart item from the customer's shopping cart.

**Setup:**
1. Register a new customer account via POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join

4. Verify cart total updated immediately after removal
5. Verify remaining items in cart are unaffected

**Validation Points:**
- Cart item successfully deleted from database
- Cart total recalculated correctly
- Empty cart state if this was the only item

- All added order items should change from 'paid' to 'shipped' status
- Item count in shipment should increase to total order items
- Shipment should remain in 'created' state (no tracking added yet)

**Validations**:
- All order items belong to same seller (validated by system)
- All order items have 'paid' status before addition
- Shipment is in 'created' state (no tracking number)

- Response status 200 OK

- snapshotStatus reflects status at time of snapshot (e.g., 'pending')
- sellerResponse contains seller's decision ('approved' or 'rejected')

- Customer can only access snapshots of their own refund requests

Test retrieving a specific administrative audit log by its unique identifier.

The admin audit log retrieval endpoint allows administrators to view individual audit log records for security and compliance purposes.

**Test Steps**:
1. Call GET /ecommerceMall/admin/admin/audit-logs/{auditLogId} with a valid, existing audit log UUID
2. Validate the response status is 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains all required fields:
   - id: UUID matching the requested audit log
   - action: string describing the administrative action performed
   - resourceType: string indicating the type of resource affected
   - resourceId: UUID of the affected resource
   - ipAddress: IP address from which the action was performed
   - createdAt: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the action occurred
   - admin: object with admin summary (id, email, name)
4. Verify optional fields are present when applicable:
   - details: additional context about the action
   - userAgent: browser/client information
5. Confirm audit logs are immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted through this endpoint

- reason should match the reason provided during promotion (or null)
- created_at timestamp should be present and valid ISO 8601 format

scenario.draft:
Test that inventory adjustment is blocked when the requested quantity would result in negative stock.

Setup sequence:
1. Admin creates a category
2. Seller registers and authenticates
3. Seller creates a product with the category
4. Seller creates a product variant

Test execution with two sequential inventory operations:

First operation - Limited restock (setup):
- quantity: 10
- operationType: "restock"
- reason: "limited stock available"
- Verify stock is now 10

Second operation - Adjustment exceeding stock (main test):
- quantity: 15 (greater than available stock of 10)
- operationType: "adjustment"
- reason: "inventory count correction"
- Verify the adjustment request is rejected with an error
- Verify variant's stock remains at 10 (unchanged)
- Verify no additional inventory record was created

Validation points:
- System prevents negative stock scenario
- Adjustment request with quantity > available stock is rejected
- Variant quantity unchanged after failed adjustment
- Error message clearly indicates insufficient stock for adjustment
- Original restock record preserved

scenario.draft:
Test scenario for customer product search with keyword query, filters, and sorting.

**Prerequisites Setup**:
1. Authenticate as customer by calling POST /ecommerceMall/auth/customer/join with valid email and password to obtain JWT token for Authorization header.

**Test Steps**:
1. Send PATCH request to /ecommerceMall/customer/products/search with Authorization header containing the customer's JWT token.
2. Include search criteria in request body:
   - Set 'q' parameter to a product name keyword (e.g., "laptop")
   - Set 'categoryId' to filter by a specific category
   - Set 'minPrice' to 100 and 'maxPrice' to 500 for price range filter
   - Set 'inStock' to true to show only products with available stock
   - Set 'sort' to 'newest' for sorting by creation date descending
   - Set 'page' to 1 and 'limit' to 20 for pagination

**Expected Validations**:
- Response status should be 200 OK
- Response body should contain 'pagination' object with 'records', 'pages', 'current', 'limit' fields
- Response body should contain 'data' array with product summaries
- Each product in 'data' array should include: id, name, basePrice, category (object with id, name), thumbnailUrl, minVariantPrice, maxVariantPrice, hasStock (should be true due to inStock filter), shopName, averageRating, reviewsCount, createdAt
- Products should match the keyword in name or description (case-insensitive partial match)
- Products should be within the specified price range
- Products should have at least one variant with stock (hasStock = true)
- Results should be sorted by newest first (createdAt descending)
- Price range display: when minVariantPrice differs from maxVariantPrice, both values should be returned to show range
- Deleted products should NOT appear in search results

scenario.draft:
Test successful checkout using the customer's default shipping address.

**Preconditions**:
- Customer is authenticated with valid JWT token
- Customer has created a shipping address and set it as default (is_default: true)
- Customer has added available product variants to cart with valid quantities

- Response returns HTTP 201 Created status
- Response contains order object with:
  - Unique order_number following format ORD-{timestamp}-{random}
  - status: "paid"

  - shipping_cost present (default 0)
  - total_amount equals subtotal + shipping_cost
  - shipping_address matches the customer's default address
  - customer matches authenticated customer
  - orderItems array contains one item per cart item with frozen unit_price
- Order item includes productSnapshot with frozen product data
- Order item includes sellerProfileSnapshot with frozen seller data
- orderItems have status: "paid"

**Post-Validation Checks**:
- Cart items are removed from cart (cart is now empty)
- Variant inventory quantity decreased by ordered quantity

scenario.draft:
Test checkout is blocked when customer has a deleted or unavailable product variant in their cart.

**Business Rule**: Deleted variants cannot be included in checkout under any circumstances. The system shall block checkout attempts that include deleted cart items.

**Test Steps**:
1. Customer calls POST /ecommerceMall/customer/payments/checkout with shippingAddressId
2. System retrieves cart and finds the variant is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null)
3. System returns 400 Bad Request with 'ITEM_UNAVAILABLE' error code

**Expected Validations**:
- Response returns 400 Bad Request with error code 'ITEM_UNAVAILABLE'
- Response includes item details identifying the unavailable item
- No order is created in the database
- Cart items remain unchanged (not cleared)
- Variant quantity remains unchanged
- Customer must remove deleted item from cart before completing checkout

**Edge Case Variations**:
- Variant exists but product is deleted
- Variant exists but product has no non-deleted variants
- Variant quantity is 0 (out of stock)

# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform - Implementation Requirements

Implement all API endpoints for the e-commerce platform with complete business logic.

## Authentication Module

### Customer Auth
- POST /auth/customer/register - Register with email/password, hash password, create customer profile
- POST /auth/customer/login - Validate credentials, return JWT token
- POST /auth/customer/change-password - Verify current password, hash and store new password
- DELETE /auth/customer/account - Soft delete: preserve orders, mark reviews as "deleted user"

### Seller Auth
- POST /auth/seller/register - Register with email/password, status=pending
- POST /auth/seller/login - Validate credentials, return JWT (only if approved)
- POST /auth/seller/change-password - Same as customer
- GET /auth/seller/approval-status - Return pending/approved/rejected
- GET /auth/seller/rejection-reason - Return rejection reason if rejected
- POST /auth/seller/reregister - Reset to pending status
- DELETE /auth/seller/account - Check no pending orders/refunds, then soft delete

### Admin Auth
- POST /auth/admin/request - Create admin request with reason
- POST /auth/admin/login - Validate, return JWT (only if isAdmin=true)
- POST /auth/admin/change-password - Update password
- GET /auth/admin/requests - List pending requests (super admin only)
- POST /auth/admin/requests/:id/approve - Approve, set isAdmin=true
- POST /auth/admin/requests/:id/reject - Reject with reason
- POST /auth/admin/promote/:userId - Set isSuperAdmin=true
- POST /auth/admin/demote/:userId - Set isSuperAdmin=false (cannot demote self)

## Customer Module

### Profile
- GET /customers/profile - Return profile with displayName, phone
- PUT /customers/profile - Update displayName, phone

### Addresses
- GET /customers/addresses - List addresses
- POST /customers/addresses - Create address (recipientName, phone, street, city, state, postalCode, country)
- PUT /customers/addresses/:id - Update address fields
- DELETE /customers/addresses/:id - Delete address
- PUT /customers/addresses/:id/default - Set as default (only one default)

## Seller Module

### Profile
- GET /sellers/profile - Return shopName, description, logo
- PUT /sellers/profile - Update fields, create snapshot before save
- GET /sellers/public/:id - Public profile view

### Products
- GET /sellers/products - List own products with pagination
- POST /sellers/products - Create product (name, description, categoryId, basePrice)
- PUT /sellers/products/:id - Update product, create snapshot
- DELETE /sellers/products/:id - Check no pending orders, delete cascades to variants/inventory
- GET /sellers/products/:id/snapshots - List snapshots

### Product Images
- POST /sellers/products/:id/images - Upload and store image URL
- PUT /sellers/products/:id/images/reorder - Update sort order
- DELETE /sellers/products/:id/images/:imageId - Delete image

### Variants
- GET /sellers/products/:id/variants - List variants
- POST /sellers/products/:id/variants - Create variant (sku, options, price, stock)
- PUT /sellers/products/:id/variants/:variantId - Update, create snapshot
- DELETE /sellers/products/:id/variants/:variantId - Check no pending orders, delete

### Inventory
- GET /sellers/variants/:id/inventory - List inventory history
- POST /sellers/variants/:id/inventory - Add record (quantity, reason)

### Orders (Seller View)
- GET /sellers/orders/items - List order items for seller's products, filterable by status
- GET /sellers/orders/items/:id - Get item details
- POST /sellers/orders/shipments - Create shipment with tracking info
- GET /sellers/orders/cancellations - List pending cancellation requests
- POST /sellers/orders/cancellations/:id/approve - Approve, refund, restore stock
- POST /sellers/orders/cancellations/:id/reject - Reject, create snapshot
- GET /sellers/orders/refunds - List pending refund requests
- POST /sellers/orders/refunds/:id/approve - Approve, process refund, restore stock
- POST /sellers/orders/refunds/:id/reject - Reject, create snapshot

### Dashboard
- GET /sellers/dashboard - Return totalProducts, totalOrderItems, pendingCancellations, pendingRefunds

## Public Product Module

### Search & Listing
- GET /products/search - Search with q, categoryId, minPrice, maxPrice, inStock, sort, pagination
- GET /products - List products with same filters
- GET /products/:id - Full product detail with variants, images, reviews, averageRating

## Wishlist Module
- GET /customers/wishlist - List wishlist products (paginated)
- POST /customers/wishlist - Add product (check not already added)
- DELETE /customers/wishlist/:productId - Remove product

## Cart Module
- GET /customers/cart - Get cart with items, subtotals, total, availability warnings
- POST /customers/cart/items - Add variant (combine quantity if same variant exists)
- PUT /customers/cart/items/:id - Update quantity
- DELETE /customers/cart/items/:id - Remove item

## Checkout & Payment Module
- GET /customers/checkout - Get checkout summary (items, address, total)
- POST /customers/checkout - Create order draft (returns orderId)
- POST /payments/order/:id/process - Process payment:
  - Success: Create order, reduce stock (create inventory records), clear cart, create order items with snapshots, status="paid"
  - Failure: Return error, no order created

## Order Module (Customer)
- GET /customers/orders - List orders (paginated, newest first)
- GET /customers/orders/:id - Order details with items, address, shipments
- POST /customers/orders/:id/items/:itemId/cancel - Create cancellation request (reason)
- POST /customers/orders/:id/items/:itemId/refund - Create refund request (reason, check within 7 days of delivery)
- POST /customers/orders/:id/shipments/:shipmentId/confirm-delivery - Mark items as delivered

## Review Module
- GET /products/:id/reviews - List reviews (newest first, paginated)
- POST /customers/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId/review - Create review (rating, text), check one per product per order
- PUT /customers/reviews/:id - Update review, create snapshot
- DELETE /customers/reviews/:id - Delete review

## Category Module
- GET /categories - List all categories with subcategories
- GET /categories/:id - Category details
- GET /categories/:id/products - Products in category
- POST /admin/categories - Create category (admin only)
- PUT /admin/categories/:id - Update category (admin only)
- DELETE /admin/categories/:id - Delete category, products become uncategorized (admin only)

## Admin Module

### Seller Management
- GET /admin/sellers - List all sellers
- GET /admin/sellers/pending - List pending approvals
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/approve - Set status=approved
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/reject - Set status=rejected with reason
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/suspend - Set isSuspended=true, hide products
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/unsuspend - Set isSuspended=false
- GET /admin/sellers/:id - Seller details

### Product Oversight
- GET /admin/products - List all products
- GET /admin/products/:id/snapshots - View any snapshot
- DELETE /admin/products/:id - Force delete

### Order Oversight
- GET /admin/orders - List all orders
- GET /admin/orders/:id - Order details
- POST /admin/orders/:id/items/:itemId/force-cancel - Force cancel, refund, restore stock
- POST /admin/orders/:id/force-cancel - Force cancel all items
- POST /admin/orders/:id/items/:itemId/force-refund - Force refund, restore stock
- POST /admin/orders/:id/force-refund - Force refund all items

### User Management
- GET /admin/customers - List customers
- GET /admin/customers/:id - Customer details
- POST /admin/customers/:id/ban - Set isBanned=true
- POST /admin/customers/:id/unban - Set isBanned=false
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/ban - Set isBanned=true
- POST /admin/sellers/:id/unban - Set isBanned=false

## Snapshot Module
- GET /snapshots/:id - View snapshot details (owner/admin only)

## Implementation Notes

1. All endpoints must be properly authenticated with JWT guards
2. Role-based access control (customer, seller, admin)
3. Input validation using class-validator DTOs
4. Transactions for operations that modify multiple tables
5. Proper error handling with appropriate HTTP status codes
6. Order status calculation: all paid→paid, any shipped→shipped, all delivered→delivered, all cancelled→cancelled, all refunded→refunded, mixed→partially_completed
7. Item status flow: paid→shipped→delivered OR paid→cancelled OR delivered→refunded
8. Average rating calculation: SUM(ratings) / COUNT(non-deleted reviews)
9. Suspended sellers: products hidden from search/listings, cannot create/edit products, can still process orders
10. Banned users cannot login
11. Soft delete for customers: orders preserved, reviews show "deleted user"
12. Soft delete for sellers: products hidden, orders preserved with snapshots

This is a Read DTO with DB-backed data and direct table mapping. Transformable - maps to ecommerce_mall_products.

IEcommerceMallCartItem.ISummary is a Read DTO for customer cart listings. Has x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_cart_items indicating direct table mapping. Contains direct fields (id, quantity, createdAt, updatedAt) from ecommerce_mall_cart_items plus computed fields and joined variant/product data. IEcommerceMallCart is a read DTO for customer shopping cart responses. The interface schema shows x-autobe-database-schema: ecommerce_mall_carts with direct field mappings (id, created_at, updated_at), belongs-to relation to customer, and has-many relation to cart items. This is a database-backed read entity that transforms ecommerce_mall_carts table data.

IEcommerceMallWishlistItem.IInvert maps to ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items. Read DTO for API response when adding product to wishlist. Direct columns: id, created_at. BELONGS-TO relations to product and wishlist. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallOrder.ISummary is a Read DTO used for paginated order listings. IEcommerceMallOrderItem is a Read DTO for individual order line item responses. It maps to ecommerce_mall_order_items table with BELONGS-TO relations to productSnapshot (product_snapshots), sellerProfileSnapshot (seller_profile_snapshots), productVariant (product_variants), and order (orders). Contains computed aggregation fields (cancellationRequestsCount, refundRequestsCount, reviewsCount). Transformable to ecommerce_mall_order_items.

IEcommerceMallShipment.ISummary is a read DTO for listing shipments with tracking info. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallShipmentItem is a read DTO for API responses showing shipment item details. IEcommerceMallProductSnapshot is a read DTO that directly maps to the ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots database table. It contains product state at snapshot time including name, description, base_price, category_name, created_at. Joins seller via FK for ISummary, variants via snapshot_id relation, and images via snapshot_id relation. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallCancellationRequest is transformable. x-autobe-database-schema shows it maps to ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots table. IEcommerceMallOrder.IInvert is a read DTO that maps to ecommerce_mall_orders table. The schema explicitly contains x-autobe-database-schema: "ecommerce_mall_orders" with JOINs to customer, shippingAddress, orderItems, and shipments. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallShipment is a complete shipment entity DTO used for API responses. Based on the x-autobe-database-schema annotation in the interface schema, it maps directly to ecommerce_mall_shipments table with fields: id, carrier, tracking_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. IEcommerceMallReview maps to ecommerce_mall_reviews table. The x-autobe-database-schema explicitly confirms ecommerce_mall_reviews table mapping. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallShipment.IInvert is a complete shipment entity for seller shipment update responses. Based on the interface schema, it maps all direct fields from ecommerce_mall_shipments table (id, carrier, tracking_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). IEcommerceMallRefundRequest maps directly to ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots table. IEcommerceMallAdminAuditLog maps directly to ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs table. It is a read-only DTO for API responses containing audit log records with admin info via JOIN. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallSellerSuspension.ISummary is a read DTO (ISummary suffix) used for API responses listing seller suspension records. It maps directly to ecommerce_mall_seller_suspensions table with relations to sellers and admins tables. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallSellerApproval is a complete seller approval entity used for API responses. IEcommerceMallAdminPromotion.ISummary is a Read DTO (ISummary suffix) used for API responses listing admin promotion/demotion audit records. IEcommerceMallProductVariant.ISummary is a Read DTO for product variant listings. Maps directly to ecommerce_mall_product_variants table with HAS-MANY relation to optionValues and BELONGS-TO relation to product. Transformable.
IEcommerceMallWishlist.ISummary maps to ecommerce_mall_wishlists. Transformable - read DTO with DB-backed data and direct table mapping.

IEcommerceMallCart.IInvert is a read DTO for displaying customer shopping cart. The schema shows x-autobe-database-schema: 'ecommerce_mall_carts'. IEcommerceMallSellerApproval.ISummary maps directly to ecommerce_mall_seller_approvals table. It is a read DTO (ISummary variant) used for listing seller approvals in admin views. Transformable.

IEcommerceMallOrder is a complete order entity for API responses. Maps to ecommerce_mall_orders table with BELONGS-TO relations to customer and shippingAddress, and HAS-MANY relations to orderItems and shipments. Transformable - read DTO backed by database with direct table mapping.
